page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz and is equipped with a 48 MB L3 cache. The system includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 2458 GB of bundled local storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 62,149.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 61,043.75. Memory performance is also highly rated, demonstrating strong large-block read and write bandwidths of 291.88 GB/sec and 134.9 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,649.0. The server excels in parallelized workloads, achieving high throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation.

Given its high resource density, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial bundled local storage, the D64d_v5 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high IOPS and balanced memory-to-CPU ratios. It is highly suitable for database operations, as evidenced by its strong PassMark database score and Redis SET performance of 62.01 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded data processing, and software compilation pipelines.
